title: CmdPal: Icons (5/n) - Move icon conversion helpers from C++ to C#
summary: The current upstream head still contains three correctness and performance issues found during the resumed review: native icon indexes above Int32.MaxValue can wrap into accepted negative indexes, the System.Drawing conversion path does not reliably preserve transparent icon pixels, and each binary icon conversion allocates large temporary buffers instead of pooling them. A clean candidate based on the exact upstream head contains the fixes and regression coverage, and the affected builds plus 16 targeted icon tests passed.

proposed_comments.title: Reject icon indexes that overflow Int32
proposed_comments.body:
### Reject icon indexes that overflow Int32

**Severity:** `high`

`ParseNativeIconIndex` currently accepts the parsed unsigned value and casts it to `int`, so an index above `Int32.MaxValue` can wrap into a negative value and be treated as a valid binary icon reference. A malformed or untrusted icon path can therefore select an unintended resource instead of taking the invalid-icon fallback. Reject values above `Int32.MaxValue` before the cast and keep boundary coverage for `2147483647`, `2147483648`, and `-2147483648`.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The fix and its boundary tests span the parser and parser-test files, so this is recorded as a coordinated general review note rather than a single safe one-line suggestion.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The fix and its boundary tests span the parser and parser-test files, so this is recorded as a coordinated general review note rather than a single safe one-line suggestion.

confidence.rationale: The overflow is directly visible in the current unsigned-to-signed cast, and the exact-head candidate adds the guard and boundary cases while passing the targeted parser tests.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve transparency when materializing binary icons
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve transparency when materializing binary icons

**Severity:** `high`

The current `System.Drawing.Icon` to `Bitmap` conversion does not reliably preserve the source icon's transparent pixels when the result is copied into a premultiplied `SoftwareBitmap`. Icons with masks can therefore render with opaque or black backgrounds in Command Palette. Render and inspect the icon mask explicitly, preserve transparent pixels, and premultiply only when needed; add an assertion that an extracted shell icon contains both transparent and visible pixels.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction replaces the native bitmap materialization path and adds pixel-level regression coverage, so it is not safe as one localized apply-ready replacement.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The correction replaces the native bitmap materialization path and adds pixel-level regression coverage, so it is not safe as one localized apply-ready replacement.

confidence.rationale: The current conversion path uses System.Drawing cloning before copying pixels into a premultiplied bitmap; the exact-head candidate's explicit mask reconstruction passed the binary icon test with transparent and visible pixels.

proposed_comments.title: Pool temporary buffers used by binary icon conversion
proposed_comments.body:
### Pool temporary buffers used by binary icon conversion

**Severity:** `medium`

Binary icon conversion allocates sizeable pixel arrays for every icon request, which adds avoidable GC pressure on the icon-loading path where many icons can be materialized during list virtualization. Rent the black and white pixel buffers from `ArrayPool<byte>` and return every rented buffer from the cleanup path, including failed native-resource creation or draw operations. Keep the conversion-content regression test so pooling cannot hide an incomplete or stale buffer.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The allocation change is coupled to the new native bitmap cleanup path and the conversion-content test, so it is recorded as a coordinated general review note.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The allocation change is coupled to the new native bitmap cleanup path and the conversion-content test, so it is recorded as a coordinated general review note.

confidence.rationale: The current implementation allocates conversion buffers per request, while the exact-head candidate pools both buffers and returns them in finally blocks; the affected project and targeted tests pass.
